clients.name: Claude Code

install.command: claude mcp add --transport http jobo-job-search https://jobs-mcp.jobo.world/mcp
install.snippet: claude mcp add --transport http jobo-job-search https://jobs-mcp.jobo.world/mcp

clients.signIn: Run claude mcp login jobo-job-search from a shell and complete the Jobo sign-in in the browser. The server connects and lists its tools without it, so Claude Code shows the server as connected either way. If you skip the sign-in, the first tool call fails with a message telling you to run /mcp, which starts the same sign-in from inside a session.
clients.verify: Run claude mcp list and check that jobo-job-search shows as connected, or open /mcp inside a session to see the server and its tools.
notes: The command adds the server for the current project only. Add --scope user to make it available in every project, or --scope project to write a shared .mcp.json.
Headless runs (claude -p) cannot complete a browser sign-in. Sign in once interactively first.

clients.name: Codex

install.command:
codex mcp add jobo-job-search --url https://jobs-mcp.jobo.world/mcp
codex mcp login jobo-job-search
install.snippet:
codex mcp add jobo-job-search --url https://jobs-mcp.jobo.world/mcp
codex mcp login jobo-job-search

clients.signIn: Run codex mcp login jobo-job-search, which opens the browser for the Jobo sign-in. Add --no-browser to print the URL instead. The server lists its tools before you sign in, but calling one needs it.
clients.verify: Run codex mcp list, or type /mcp in the Codex TUI to see the active MCP servers.
notes: codex mcp add does not sign you in; codex mcp login is a separate step.
The Codex CLI, IDE extension and desktop app share ~/.codex/config.toml, so one setup covers all three.

clients.name: Qwen Code

install.command: qwen mcp add --transport http jobo-job-search https://jobs-mcp.jobo.world/mcp
install.snippet: qwen mcp add --transport http jobo-job-search https://jobs-mcp.jobo.world/mcp

clients.signIn: Start qwen and open /mcp, then select the server in the dialog to sign in: Qwen Code discovers the server's OAuth endpoints, registers itself and runs the browser sign-in. The server connects and lists its tools before you sign in, so do this before the first search.
clients.verify: Run /mcp inside Qwen Code to see the server's status and tool list, or qwen mcp list from the shell.
notes: The command writes to ~/.qwen/settings.json. Add --scope project to write .qwen/settings.json instead.
The sign-in callback uses a local port and needs a browser on the same machine, so it does not work over plain SSH.

clients.name: OpenCode

install.command:
opencode mcp add jobo-job-search --global --url https://jobs-mcp.jobo.world/mcp
opencode mcp auth jobo-job-search
install.snippet:
opencode mcp add jobo-job-search --global --url https://jobs-mcp.jobo.world/mcp
opencode mcp auth jobo-job-search

clients.signIn: Run opencode mcp auth jobo-job-search, which opens the browser. Inside OpenCode, /mcps lists the server and starts the same sign-in. The server connects and lists its tools before you sign in, so do this before the first search.
clients.verify: Run opencode mcp list and check that jobo-job-search shows as connected. It can show as connected before you have signed in, because the server lists its tools without it.
notes: Without --global the server is added to the current project's opencode.json.
Over SSH or in a container the browser callback page will not load. Copy that page's URL and paste it into the sign-in prompt.
These commands are from the current OpenCode documentation. On OpenCode V1, add the server to the config file by hand, then run opencode mcp auth.

clients.name: Goose

install.snippet:
extensions:
  jobo-job-search:
    name: jobo-job-search
    type: streamable_http
    uri: https://jobs-mcp.jobo.world/mcp
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

clients.signIn: The server connects and lists its tools before you sign in, and asks for sign-in the first time a tool is called. Goose then registers itself with the server and opens an OAuth window in your browser. Approve access there.
clients.verify: Check that the extension is listed and enabled under goose configure → Toggle Extensions, or in the Extensions list in goose Desktop.
notes: The endpoint key is uri, not url, and the type is streamable_http.
Prefer a wizard? Run goose configure, select Add Extension, choose Remote Extension (Streamable HTTP) and enter the same URL.

clients.name: Amp
clients.signIn: The server connects and lists its tools before you sign in, and asks for sign-in the first time a tool is called. Amp then opens the Jobo sign-in page in your browser; approve access there.
clients.verify: Run amp mcp doctor to see the server's status.
notes: A server added to workspace settings (.amp/settings.json) must be approved before it runs: amp mcp approve jobo-job-search.
To sign in again, run amp mcp oauth logout jobo-job-search and restart Amp.

clients.name: Warp

uiSteps: Open Settings → Agents → MCP servers and click + Add.
Paste the JSON below and save.
Start the server from the MCP servers page if it is not already running.

clients.signIn: The server connects and lists its tools before you sign in, and asks for sign-in the first time an agent calls a tool. Warp then opens the Jobo sign-in in your browser. After you approve, Warp stores the credentials on your device and reuses them.
clients.verify: On the MCP servers page the server shows as running, with its list of tools. Use View Logs on the server's row if it fails.

clients.name: Gemini CLI

install.command: gemini mcp add --transport http --scope user jobo-job-search https://jobs-mcp.jobo.world/mcp
install.snippet: gemini mcp add --transport http --scope user jobo-job-search https://jobs-mcp.jobo.world/mcp

clients.signIn: Inside Gemini CLI, run /mcp auth jobo-job-search, which opens a browser for the Jobo sign-in. The server connects and lists its tools before you sign in, so do this before the first search.
clients.verify: Run /mcp in the CLI to see the server as connected with its tools, or gemini mcp list from the shell.
notes: --scope user writes ~/.gemini/settings.json. Without it the server is added to the current project only.
The sign-in needs a local browser, so it fails over SSH and in containers without one.

clients.name: Augment

install.command: auggie mcp add jobo-job-search --command npx --args "-y mcp-remote https://jobs-mcp.jobo.world/mcp"
install.snippet: auggie mcp add jobo-job-search --command npx --args "-y mcp-remote https://jobs-mcp.jobo.world/mcp"

clients.signIn: The bridge connects and lists the tools before you sign in. The first time a tool is called, mcp-remote opens the Jobo sign-in page in your default browser and holds the call while you approve access, then runs it. It caches the tokens, so later starts are silent.
clients.verify: Run /mcp inside an Auggie session to see the status of configured servers, or auggie mcp list from the shell.
notes: The command saves to ~/.augment/settings.json. Pass --project to write .augment/settings.json instead.
Auggie can also add the URL directly (--transport http --url), but its MCP documentation does not describe the OAuth sign-in for remote servers, so this guide uses the bridge.

mcp-remote waits 30 seconds for the sign-in by default. If the first call fails because you were still signing in, ask again, or give yourself longer by adding --auth-timeout and a number of seconds to the args.

clients.name: Conductor

install.command: claude mcp add --transport http -s user jobo-job-search https://jobs-mcp.jobo.world/mcp
install.snippet: claude mcp add --transport http -s user jobo-job-search https://jobs-mcp.jobo.world/mcp

clients.signIn: Run claude mcp login jobo-job-search in a terminal and complete the Jobo sign-in in the browser. Conductor's MCP status dialog (the plug icon in the composer, or /mcp-status) offers the same sign-in on the server's row when the server needs it. The server connects and lists its tools before you sign in, so it can show as connected before you have.
clients.verify: Click the plug icon in the composer, or run /mcp-status, and refresh the status.
notes: Conductor has no MCP configuration of its own. Claude Code sessions use Claude Code's servers and Codex sessions use Codex's, so for Codex sessions follow the Codex setup instead.
A session started before the server was added does not see it. Refresh the MCP status and start a new session.
Enterprise data privacy mode in Conductor disables custom MCP servers.

clients.name: Cline
clients.signIn: Cline runs a browser authorization for the server when it asks for sign-in, which is the first time a tool is called. In the Cline CLI you can start or repeat it yourself: run cline mcp and choose Authorize OAuth, then approve access in the browser.
clients.verify: Open MCP Servers in Cline and confirm jobo-job-search is enabled and its tools are listed.
notes: Keep "type": "streamableHttp". Without it Cline falls back to the legacy SSE transport, which this server does not offer.
The file above is the Cline CLI's. In the IDE extension, open MCP Servers → Remote Servers and enter the same name and URL with the Streamable HTTP transport.

clients.name: Roo Code
clients.signIn: The bridge connects and lists the tools before you sign in. The first time a tool is called, mcp-remote opens the Jobo sign-in page in your default browser and holds the call while you approve access, then runs it. It caches the tokens, so later starts are silent.
clients.verify: Open the MCP view in Roo Code and confirm jobo-job-search is listed, enabled, and shows its tools.
notes: Open the global file from Roo Code's MCP view with Edit Global MCP. Edit Project MCP opens .roo/mcp.json.
On Windows, launch through cmd: set command to cmd and put /c, npx, -y, mcp-remote and the URL in args.

mcp-remote waits 30 seconds for the sign-in by default. If the first call fails because you were still signing in, ask again, or give yourself longer by adding --auth-timeout and a number of seconds to the args.

clients.name: Amazon Q Developer

In the CLI, once Amazon Q reports that the server requires authentication, run /mcp, open the URL it prints and sign in while the session stays open. In the IDE, Amazon Q opens the browser authorization when the server asks for it.

Organisations on the Pro tier can turn MCP off or restrict it to an allow-list, in which case a server you add will not load.

clients.name: Crush

install.snippet: mcp add jobo-job-search --type http --url "https://jobs-mcp.jobo.world/mcp" --oauth true --sessionless true

clients.signIn: The server connects and lists its tools before you sign in, and asks for sign-in the first time a tool is called. With --oauth true, Crush then registers itself with the server and runs the authorization flow. Complete the Jobo sign-in in the browser.
clients.verify: Start crush and confirm jobo-job-search appears as connected. crush logs shows connection errors if it does not.
notes: crushrc is a shell-style file, not JSON. Add the line as it is.
--sessionless true tells Crush the server does not issue session IDs, which this one does not.

clients.name: Cursor
clients.signIn: The server connects and lists its tools before you sign in, and asks for sign-in the first time a tool is called. Cursor then opens the Jobo sign-in page in your browser. Sign in, approve access and return to Cursor.
clients.verify: Open Customize in the Cursor sidebar and check that jobo-job-search is listed and switched on. If it is not, open the Output panel and pick MCP Logs.
notes: A remote entry needs only url. No type field is required.
Enterprise admins can restrict which MCP servers run, in which case a server you add may be blocked.

clients.name: VS Code
clients.signIn: The server connects and lists its tools before you sign in, and asks for sign-in the first time a tool is called. Complete the sign-in when VS Code prompts for it, or choose Authenticate in the server's actions when it is offered, then finish the Jobo sign-in in the browser.
clients.verify: Ask Copilot a question that needs job data and expand the tool call in the conversation to confirm it came from jobo-job-search.
notes: Prefer the guided flow? With Copilot selected in the Chat view, run Chat: Open Customizations, select MCP Servers, then Add Server. Choose HTTP, enter the URL and the server ID jobo-job-search, and select Global, then Copilot Global.
The older .vscode/mcp.json format, with a top-level servers key, belongs to VS Code's Local harness. The documentation marks it as deprecated and due for removal in February 2027.
An organisation policy can restrict MCP servers to an allow-list.

clients.name: Visual Studio
clients.signIn: The server connects and lists its tools before you sign in, and asks for sign-in the first time a tool is called. When it does, open the .mcp.json file in Visual Studio and select Authentication Required in the CodeLens above the server entry, then complete the Jobo sign-in in the browser.
clients.verify: In the Copilot chat pane, choose Agent mode and open Tools. The jobo-job-search tools are listed there; they are off by default and must be ticked before use.
notes: Requires Visual Studio 2026, or Visual Studio 2022 version 17.14 or later.
The top-level key is servers, not mcpServers.
If the CodeLens above the server entry is missing, enable it under Tools → Options → Text Editor → CodeLens.

clients.name: Windsurf
clients.signIn: The server connects and lists its tools before you sign in, and asks for sign-in the first time a tool is called. The server then appears under Customize → MCPs with a Needs authentication state: click Authenticate and complete the Jobo sign-in in the browser.
clients.verify: Customize → MCPs lists jobo-job-search as enabled, without the Needs authentication state.
notes: Windsurf has been renamed Devin Desktop. The file above is the location its current documentation gives.
From the Devin CLI: devin mcp add jobo-job-search https://jobs-mcp.jobo.world/mcp -s user, then devin mcp login jobo-job-search.

clients.name: Kiro
clients.signIn: The server connects and lists its tools before you sign in, and asks for sign-in the first time a tool is called. Kiro then runs the browser sign-in: it registers itself and opens the Jobo authorization page. If a token later expires, use the Re-authenticate button in the MCP panel.
clients.verify: Check the MCP servers tab in the Kiro panel to confirm jobo-job-search is connected.
notes: MCP support must be switched on: open Settings, search for MCP and enable it.
Open the file from the Command Palette with Kiro: Open user MCP config (JSON).

clients.name: Zed
clients.signIn: The server connects and lists its tools before you sign in, and asks for sign-in the first time a tool is called. Because the entry has no Authorization header, Zed then prompts you to authenticate. Follow the prompt and finish the Jobo sign-in in the browser.
clients.verify: Open Settings → AI → MCP Servers. The indicator next to jobo-job-search is green when the server is active.
notes: Open the file with the zed: open settings file action.
The key is context_servers, not mcpServers. Merge the entry into your existing settings rather than replacing the file.
Or use the UI: Settings → AI → MCP Servers → Add Server → Add Remote Server.

clients.name: JetBrains IDEs

uiSteps: Open Settings → Tools → AI Assistant → Model Context Protocol (MCP) and click Add.
Choose the STDIO connection and paste the JSON below.
Set the server level to global or the current project, click OK, then Apply.

clients.signIn: The bridge connects and lists the tools before you sign in. The first time a tool is called, mcp-remote opens the Jobo sign-in page in your default browser and holds the call while you approve access, then runs it. It caches the tokens, so later starts are silent.

Click Add, then Create Manually.
Paste the JSON below and click Confirm.

clients.name: ChatGPT

uiSteps: On ChatGPT web, open Plugins.
Select the plus button, then Add custom MCP server.
Enter a name and, optionally, a description.
Under Connection, enter the server URL below and set authentication to OAuth.
Review the risk warning, tick I understand and want to continue, select Create as a plugin, then install it.

clients.signIn: Complete the Jobo authorization prompt in the browser when ChatGPT asks for it.
clients.verify: The review step after Create as a plugin lists the tools ChatGPT discovered. Then start a new conversation, type @ and select the plugin.
notes: Custom MCP server connections are available on ChatGPT Business and Enterprise/Edu, on the web. On Business, only admins and owners can create them.
The server implements the search and fetch tools, the pair deep research uses.

clients.name: Claude

uiSteps: Open Connectors at claude.ai/customize/connectors.
Select Add, then Add custom connector.
Enter a name and the server URL below, then click Continue.
Keep the detected authentication options and click Add.

clients.signIn: Claude asks for sign-in the first time it uses a Jobo tool: a Connect card appears in the conversation. Click Connect and complete the Jobo sign-in in the popup, and Claude retries the call. If the connector's entry under Connectors shows a Connect button, clicking it signs you in ahead of time.
clients.verify: In a chat, click + and check the connector is switched on under Connectors.
notes: Custom connectors are available on every plan. The Free plan allows one.
On Team and Enterprise, an Owner adds the connector under Organization settings → Connectors, and members then click Connect.
The connector is account-level: once added it works in claude.ai, Claude Desktop and the mobile apps.

clients.name: Perplexity

uiSteps: Open Plugins in the sidebar.
Select Add custom, then Add MCP connector, and choose Remote.
Enter a name and the server URL below.
Under Advanced, set Authentication to OAuth and Transport to Streamable HTTP.
Tick the checkbox acknowledging that custom connectors can introduce risks, then select Add.

clients.signIn: Select the connector's card on the Plugins page and complete the Jobo sign-in in the browser. The server lists its tools before you sign in, so the connector can look ready before you have.
clients.verify: The connector is listed on the Plugins page without an error tag.
notes: In the Mac app the path is Add custom, then Connector, then Add MCP connector.

In an organization, members can add a connector only when an administrator has turned on Allow members to add custom connectors. An administrator adds one for everyone under Organization settings → Connectors, where it starts turned off.
Perplexity's help centre does not say which plans include custom connectors.
